newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Bank Negara strikes at ringgit speculators.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank Negara strikes at ringgit speculators.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank on Tuesday intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to flush out ringgit speculators after defending the currency for nearly two weeks, dealers and analysts said.
They said Bank Negara's action sent the dollar down about 200 points against the ringgit within an hour.

Dealers said Bank Negara began hitting the market just after 0800 GMT in lots of $50 million each time. "They did not face much resistance until dollar/ringgit came down to 2.5100," said a dealer with a Singapore-based U.S. bank.
At 2.5100, there was some resistance and dollar/ringgit climbed back to 2.5145 before the central bank struck again around 0930 GMT, dealers said.
"It was amazing, it was as if everyone (speculators) had laid down arms after all the efforts (to pull down the ringgit)," said the U.S. bank dealer.

He said the volumes were not large throughout the afternoon and if Bank Negara stayed in the market in London and New York, where liquidity was low, it could effectively drive out speculative short ringgit positions from the market.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5060/70 to a dollar at 1130 GMT.

Dealers said they were not surprised over the central bank's action as dollar/ringgit was trading very close to 2.5250, the level at which Bank Negara had aggressively defended the ringgit, for most of the day.
Before the intervention, offshore players out of London were seen testing the authorities after acquiring ringgit through swaps to run their long dollar/ringgit positions, they said.

"It was a question of who would act or give way first. The battle may have just begun but Bank Negara has demonstrated it's not going to hold back its punches," said research house MMS International in its market commentary.
Some dealers said the central bank could have sold more than $2 billion since last week to defend the ringgit.
Last Wednesday, Bank Negara intervened in the foreign exchange market using its own name for the first time in many years, against its usual practice of using a broker or a bank.
The central bank could not be reached for comment. It does not usually comment on its open market operations.
"The message is: speculators, don't mess around with central banks," said Jimmy Koh, economist with research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
"This move to wipe out speculators has been on the authorities' agenda," he said.
Dealers and analysts said it was likely the central bank, after squeezing speculators in the spot market, will come with another squeeze in the forward market.

"This will force these players who have borrowed ringgit at exorbitant levels to liquidate their positions. This effectively will flush out speculators with dollar/ringgit outright positions from the market," Koh said.
The authorities had expressed their concern over local banks' active involvement in the forward market.
Dealers said a fresh attack on the Malaysian currency had looked imminent as speculators were building up long ringgit positions on the swaps.
Such a position would allow speculators to sell ringgit without worrying about being squeezed by the central bank.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
